summary.text: FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity and measure the effectiveness of gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6. Recorded results include one methanol test point in a CO2/N2 atmosphere from a presentation, and individual rows of the official FLEX experimental table; no processed document reports measured suppressant effectiveness for SF6.

fuels.text: Methanol droplet in the reported FLEX test point (FLEX-145).

geometry.text: Many planned tests use free droplets rather than fiber-supported droplets.

oxygen.text: Reported FLEX testing used O2 concentrations from 13% to 21% with CO2 / N2 diluent mixtures. Test point FLEX-145 used 20% O2.

pressure.text: Test point FLEX-145 was at 1.0 atm. The plan selects test pressures of 0.5 to 1.5 atm for LOI tests.

flow.text: The plan applies a small, sub-buoyant convective flow by translating the droplet at a slow, uniform speed near the end of some tests.

gravity.text: Microgravity; the investigation aims to map flammability limits in microgravity environments.

measurements.text: Planned measurements include droplet burning rates, flame extinction behavior, heat radiation, soot levels, and temperature profiles; the presentation reports backlit droplet imaging and OH* chemiluminescence imaging.

hardware.text: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA).

claims.text: The investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity and measure the effectiveness of gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6.

The investigation hypothesizes that the lack of buoyant convection in microgravity leads to significant differences in flammability limits and suppression efficacy of fire suppressant agents compared to normal gravity.

The presentation on water absorption and evaporation in methanol droplet combustion reports that a methanol droplet in the FLEX-145 test (1.0 atm, 20% O2 / 75% CO2 / 5% N2) had an initial diameter Do of 3.38 mm, a D ext of 1.66 at visible flame extinction (unit not shown on that line), and a burning rate constant K of 0.44 m2/s.

The presentation on water absorption and evaporation in methanol droplet combustion reports that OH* chemiluminescence images from the FLEX LLUV camera provide information on the water flux transition point in methanol droplet combustion.

The test plan states that for fire safety the goal of an agent in a total flooding application is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI, so extinction data of this kind could inform suppression design.

FLEX test #226 (identifier H03M101) in the FLEX experimental table records a methanol droplet at 759.2 mmHg in an ambient with 0.18 O mole fraction, 0.67 N and 0.15 He (CO column 0), with an initial droplet diameter of 2.79 mm, a visible flame extinction diameter of 1.3 mm, a burn time of 12.5 s, and test end recorded as Extinction.

FLEX test #94 (identifier C08H101) in the FLEX experimental table records a heptane droplet at 533.6 mmHg in an ambient with 0.24 O mole fraction, 0.56 N and 0.2 in the column labeled 'CO initial ambient composition' (He 0), with an initial droplet diameter of 3.53 mm, a visible flame extinction diameter of 2.76 mm, a burn time of 10.1 s, and test end recorded as Extinction.

conditions.text: Methanol droplet at 1.0 atm in 20% O2 / 75% CO2 / 5% N2. It is part of FLEX testing with O2 from 13% to 21% in CO2 / N2 mixtures.
Methanol droplet at 759.2 mmHg with 0.18 O, 0.67 N and 0.15 He mole fractions (FLEX test #226).
Heptane droplet at 533.6 mmHg with 0.24 O, 0.56 N and 0.2 in the CO-labeled column (FLEX test #94).

limitations.text: The presentation's extinction result covers one methanol test point in CO2/N2; the presentation lists extending the analysis to the full range of FLEX methanol data as future work. The table row for FLEX test #226 is a single recorded run. The row for FLEX test #94 is likewise a single recorded run; no trend across runs is stated or claimed.

No processed document text reports measured FLEX suppressant effectiveness for SF6 (He appears only as an ambient component in individual table rows). The MEC table in the test plan is from cup burner flames (Takahashi et al., 2004), not a FLEX result.
Cool flames are mentioned only in the metadata research-impacts field; no processed document text gives a measured cool-flame result, so none is recorded as an observation.
The color-camera analysis from the ground-based Zero Gravity Facility is described as preliminary.

modeling_resources.description: FLEX experimental table of test conditions that could support future predictive modeling of droplet extinction; no model is claimed.
